What degraded

  • Frame 9 shipped as a pixel holdout after the third pixel round: its powder coat runs bright on the mast and battery. It is one of the three preflight frames and was kept as the accepted review saw it.
  • Frame 3 moved from GRID to OBJECT_AND_CAPTION, because the GRID count gate reads a lit apron as one silhouette and a dark apron left the carts in a void. Queued with the gate.
  • Frame 5 keeps a different tool's published test, labelled as a different tool. All three round 3 judges would cut it.
  • The weekly machine pass was not due. The last ran on October 7th.

Named here rather than left out. A run that quietly ships less than it planned teaches nobody anything.

Post this

Upload the PDF to LinkedIn as a document, title it Asked inside the chart. UTMB's OpenEvidence account beside Texas law, paste the post copy under it, then paste the first comment within a minute of posting.

carousel.pdf   contact sheet   the site

1. The post copy

A Texas statute and a UTMB release both describe AI in the health record.

UTMB in Galveston put OpenEvidence inside its health record in March. Clinicians get answers with citations. More than half of them use it for "clinical decision support," UTMB said on September 22nd.

Since September 1st, 2025, Sec. 183.005 of the Health and Safety Code has said a practitioner who uses AI for "diagnostic purposes" must disclose that use to patients. The record here can't say whether the section reaches this use.

A patient can ask in the exam room. The UT System Regents meet November 18th to 19th in Austin. The public may testify on a topic the agenda lists. A speaker sends the board's General Counsel a name and topic at least 24 hours ahead.

Will the November agenda list AI in the health record?

#UTMB #Galveston #UTSystem

2. The first comment

Notes

The record, first. 67 items were due. 17 were confirmed and stamped by reverify, 30 more by hand on their own sources, and 20 got a dated unconfirmed line because every source behind them refused. Boundaries were measured on Williamson County and Brownsville, and both items carry a blocks_every_client block. tx-2026-0027 was re-measured after CI's staleness gate refused it and stamped on the city's own site, which carries no written outcome. PR 415 then landed on main with the CivicClerk minutes, which record unanimous approval of the amended Compal agreement, and its version of the item was taken whole at the merge. Three items were admitted: tx-2026-0208 UTMB and OpenEvidence, tx-2026-0209 Kodiak and Charger USA, tx-2026-0210 UT REAL Health AI with Abridge. A fourth, UTSA's flood sensor, was withdrawn when Codex found it duplicated tx-2026-0141. Codex's other findings on the pull request were fixed before the merge, and CI's deciders gate caught a decider name, also fixed. The deck. tx-2026-0208. UTMB says OpenEvidence has run inside its health record since March and that more than half of its clinicians use it. The release prints no count, no total and no accuracy figure, and never uses the word diagnostic. The deck sets that beside Sec. 183.005, which binds a practitioner who uses AI for diagnostic purposes to disclose it to patients, and never joins the two. It closes on the Regents' November 18th to 19th meeting and how to testify. Selection. UTSA's flood sensor was refused by the thirty day rule on claims no. 46 carried and never printed. That is queued as a gate firing wrongly. The panel. Round 1 scored 6.86 with one hard fail: slide 6's headline "UTMB's other AI contract" implied an OpenEvidence contract no source shows. It became "UTMB's other AI platform". Round 2 scored 6.992 under the 7.7 rung. Round 3 scored 6.84 at the cap, judges 7.03, 6.78 and 6.64, no hard fail, so the finished deck ships 1.16 under the 8.0 top rung. The art median is 6.0. All three judges charge the middle frames: the barrier on 4 and 5 reads as stacked slabs, the columns on 6 as crates, and the statute page on 7 sits outside the deck. All three would cut frame 5's borrowed radiomics bars, the study no. 23 ran on September 13th, and all three named the instrument as no. 27's. Worth knowing before posting. The labels on slides 1 and 9 say 100 lights, and the frames now refuse to render unless exactly 100 land inside them. Slide 7 and the caption say the record can't say whether Sec. 183.005 reaches this use, which is the fact check's own boundary. Did the run stop for a human. No. The final reading, taken after the last merge of main and before the email, measured 1,834 tool calls and none waited on a human. 557 waited on the auto mode classifier, the longest 11.9 seconds, timed by the log and not a person. The no-stall hook was armed at 06:20:32 UTC, judged the session unattended (CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ATTENDED=0, the host's own value 0) and refused nothing. CI on the pull request. The gates job went red once on the ownership check, because an owner commit to .claude/settings.json landed on main at 11:36 UTC and CI judged it against the branch's lane through a stale base. Merging main cleared it. PR 415 then landed on main and conflicted on the docket and the field log. Its versions of tx-2026-0027 and tx-2026-0062 were taken whole, the field log kept both sections in order, and docs was rebuilt on the merged tree. The machine. The weekly pass was not due. Four items were queued. The article screenshot item reached repeat 2, so the pass is due tomorrow.

This is a draft. Nothing was sent. The deck is already merged to main, so these links are live. Posting is the only step left, and it is yours.
